personal_item_dimensions.notes: Ryanair states the same small cabin bag in two axis orders on two of its own pages. Bag Policy: "All fares include one small personal bag (40 x 30 x 20 cm) that must fit under the seat." Fare bundles: "It's our cheapest fare and includes 1 Small Cabin Bag (40x20x30cm), which must fit under the seat in front of you." Same three measurements, different order — so probably one bag described inconsistently rather than two bags. NOT normalised, because which face is the height decides whether a given case fits a sizer. Resolve against a sizer diagram or the booking flow, or report it to Ryanair. Sources: https://help.ryanair.com/hc/en-gb/articles/12888036565521-Ryanair-s-Bag-Policy and https://help.ryanair.com/hc/en-gb/articles/12888555638161-What-are-Ryanair-s-fare-bundle-options

priority_cabin_bag_dimensions.notes: CANDIDATE 55x40x20cm — "This allows you to carry a small personal bag (40 x 30 x 20 cm), which must fit under the seat in front of you and a 10kg bag (55x40x20cm) onboard, to be stored in the overhead locker." Appears identically on the fare bundles page. Source: https://help.ryanair.com/hc/en-gb/articles/12888036565521-Ryanair-s-Bag-Policy

priority_cabin_bag_weight.notes: CANDIDATE 10kg — "Priority boarding with a second 10kg cabin bag." AMBIGUOUS: 10kg also appears as a checked-bag tier in the same sentence ("checked bags of 10kg, 20kg (up to 3), or 23kg"), so this candidate is listed under checked_bag_tiers as well. Deciding which is which is a judgement about Ryanair's product, not a parse. Source: https://help.ryanair.com/hc/en-gb/articles/12888036565521-Ryanair-s-Bag-Policy

infant_allowance.notes: CANDIDATE 5kg — "Infants have no cabin allowance but may bring a 5kg baby bag and two baby equipment items free." The "two baby equipment items" count was not extracted (written as a word, not a digit) — worth capturing by hand. Source: https://help.ryanair.com/hc/en-gb/articles/12888036565521-Ryanair-s-Bag-Policy

included_checked_allowance.value: None — no checked bag is included in any fare
included_checked_allowance.notes: Every tier is described as an addition: 'you can add a 10kg Check-in Bag to your booking'. No fare includes checked baggage.

purchasable_tiers.value: 10 kg · 20 kg (up to 3 per booking) · 23 kg (up to 1 per booking)
purchasable_tiers.notes: Verbatim: '20kg Check-in Bag… Passengers can purchase up to 3 checked bags of 20kg on their booking. 23kg Check-in Bag… up to 1 checked bags of 23kg.' No per-booking limit is stated for the 10kg tier.

excess_fees.notes: No source. The baggage_fees URL is a help-centre category index, not an article — captured at 748 chars, below the threshold. Needs a real fees article URL.

basic_fare_inclusions.notes: CANDIDATES 40x20x30cm (see the personal_item_dimensions dispute), 55x40x20cm, 10kg, 20kg. "It's our cheapest fare and includes 1 Small Cabin Bag (40x20x30cm), which must fit under the seat in front of you, with no additional baggage allowance." and "This fare includes a standard seat and gives you a baggage allowance of 1 Small Cabin Bag onboard and 1 20kg Check-in bag." The fare TIER NAMES were not extracted — they are prose, not measurements — so which bundle each figure belongs to still has to be read off the page. Source: https://help.ryanair.com/hc/en-gb/articles/12888555638161-What-are-Ryanair-s-fare-bundle-options
